{{Short description|French mathematician}}
[[Image:Dominique Bakry.jpg|thumb|Dominique Bakry (2009).]]
'''Roger-Dominique Bakry''' (born 12 December 1954), known as '''Dominique Bakry''', is a French mathematician, a professor at the [[Université Paul-Sabatier]] in Toulouse, and a senior member of [[Institut Universitaire de France]].

Bakry graduated from {{Interlanguage link multi|ENS Saint-Cloud|fr}}, and prepared his PhD under the advisory of [[Paul-André Meyer]] and [[Marc Yor]].<ref>{{Cite web|url = http://genealogy.ams.org/id.php?id=60927|title = Dominique Bakry|date = |accessdate = |website = Mathematical Genealogy Project|publisher = |last = |first = }}</ref> Before coming to Toulouse, he was chargé de recherches at CNRS in [[Université Louis Pasteur]] of Strasbourg. His scientific work is at the interface of Analysis, Probability, and Geometry. His most influential works concern Riesz transforms and Markov semigroups. He gave his name to the Bakry-Émery criterion, developed in collaboration with [[Michel Émery]] and published in 1984,<ref>[http://sfb1060.iam.uni-bonn.de/project-groups/project-group-c/c01/ Feng-Yu Wang, "Functional Inequalities on Arbitrary Riemannian Manifolds"]. Accessed 3 December 2014</ref> and linked more generally to the curvature-dimension criterion.<ref>[http://www.math.ucsb.edu/~wei/paper/Wei-Wylie.pdf Guofang Wei & Will Wylie, "Comparison Geometry for the Bakry-Emery Ricci Tensor"]. Accessed 2 December 2014</ref>
